On the DreamStation, SmartRamp mode differs from standard ramp mode in how it manages pressure during the ramp period. SmartRamp mode maintains a constant lower pressure until the device detects the need for more pressure (specifically detecting airflow changes), allowing users to fall asleep to lower pressures. In contrast, standard ramp mode increases pressure at a steady rate until it reaches the prescription setting. This makes SmartRamp more responsive to the user's actual needs rather than following a fixed pressure increase schedule.

The ResMed device with a therapy algorithm designed specifically for women is the AirSense 10 AutoSet for Her. The purpose of the EZ-Start feature on the DreamStation CPAP Pro is to provide automatic, personalized adjustments to CPAP pressure designed to help patients gradually acclimate to their prescribed level of therapy. This feature helps new CPAP users adjust to their treatment by automatically adjusting the pressure over a period of up to 30 days.

The 135-degree angle in the submersed tubing of the Seattle-PAP bubble CPAP system is designed to increase the amplitude of oscillations. This design feature enhances the pressure oscillations that are characteristic of bubble CPAP therapy.

The ResMed AutoRamp feature relies on sleep onset detection to know when to ramp up to the prescribed pressure. According to the knowledge graph, AutoRamp is a feature with sleep onset detection that starts with low pressure and ramps up to prescribed pressure once the patient falls asleep.

The EPR (Expiratory Pressure Relief) feature on the ResMed AirSense 11 makes it easier to breathe out and helps users get used to therapy. It provides expiratory pressure relief during exhalation, reducing the pressure when the user breathes out.
